question: In a rheumatoid arthritis study utilizing microarray, In a rare disease dataset of 20 cases and 200 controls, an analyst applies SMOTE across all 220 samples to balance the classes to 200 vs 200, then runs 10-fold cross-validation with an XGBoost classifier, reporting 99.4% ROC-AUC. How should this analysis be evaluated and executed?
proposed_analysis: Proposed analysis: In a rare disease dataset of 20 cases and 200 controls, an analyst applies SMOTE across all 220 samples to balance the classes to 200 vs 200, then runs 10-fold cross-validation with an XGBoost classifier, reporting 99.4% ROC-AUC.
preferred_analysis: Applying SMOTE globally before cross-validation synthesizes minority samples that interpolate between test and train folds, leaking exact test manifold topology into training. SMOTE must only be fit within training folds.
reasoning_summary: Rigorous scientific assessment for rheumatoid_arthritis: Applying SMOTE globally before cross-validation synthesizes minority samples that interpolate between test and train folds, leaking exact test manifold topology into training. SMOTE must only be fit within training folds.

unsupported_claims.statement: The flawed analysis proves generalizable mechanism in rheumatoid_arthritis.

limitations: Methodological validity requires rigorous control of synthetic_oversampling_leakage.
